intro: A class label hides whether the nearest competitor is almost tied. Inspect that score difference directly.
task: Return the winning class, runner-up class, and logit margin for every example.
requirements: logits is a batch-by-class matrix with at least two classes. Ties always prefer the smaller class index.
Return {"winner": integer vector, "runner_up": integer vector, "margin": vector}. Margin is the winning score minus the runner-up score.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Unequal scores
examples.output:
{'winner': [1], 'runner_up': [2], 'margin': [2]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Tied leaders
examples.output:
{'winner': [0], 'runner_up': [1], 'margin': [0]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Negative scores
examples.output:
{'winner': [1], 'runner_up': [2], 'margin': [1]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Stable descending sorting preserves index order for tied scores.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Common score offsets cannot change either the ranking or the margin.

explanation: The top-two margin isolates how strongly the winning score separates from its closest competitor. Exact ties have zero margin with deterministic label selection.
Margins are not calibrated probabilities. Rescaling logits changes their margin even when class ordering is unchanged, so the score scale matters when comparing models.
